common:
You are a lane worker in the prime-agent Rust rewrite. Read ~/prime-agent-rs/MISSION.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/MODEL-SURFACE.md first.

Rules:
- TS reference: ~/prime-agent (read-only, never modify). Read the TS files in full before porting behavior. The installed TS binary `prime-agent` on PATH is ground truth for parity.
- Work ONLY in your worktree (given below). Commit in small increments on your lane branch. Push your branch and open a PR (gh) when done, targeting main. NEVER touch .github/ or main.
- No stubs, no todo!()/unimplemented!(), no swallowed errors. anyhow::Result propagation is fine.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` must pass in your worktree before you push. Keep every commit compiling.
- Prefer tokio/serde ecosystem deps only. This box has 4 vCPU/16GB: run cargo with `-j4` if memory pressure appears; heavy parallel builds are still fine.

When done: push branch, open PR with summary, then reply to parent (await agent_message.send(receiver_role='parent')) with PR URL, verifier evidence, and ambiguities. If blocked, reply early instead of stalling. Your provider requests may be aborted by sandbox infra kills; if that happens you will be nudged to resume — continue from where you left off.



ARCHITECTURE OWNERSHIP RULES (mandatory, from MISSION.md):
- Your crate owns exactly its declared area; see your crate README (scope/non-goals/public API) - write/extend it as part of your lane.
- pa-types is the ONLY shared crate. No other cross-crate types.
- Internals are pub(crate); cross-crate access goes through minimal public APIs only.
- Layered dependency direction (cycles forbidden): pa-types <- pa-ai <- pa-agent <- pa-core <- pa-daemon; pa-tui depends on pa-types only; pa-cli composes everything.
- No god-modules: if your change starts cutting through many subsystems, fix the boundary instead.
- Your PR must keep Cargo.toml true to this direction and must not add cross-crate internal access.


CODEX REFERENCE (new, in MISSION.md): OpenAI Codex Rust harness cloned at ~/codex (read-only, Apache 2.0 - study freely, attribute if you port specific code). Use it for internals that are easy to get wrong: token counting, KV-cacheable prefix maintenance across turns, streaming provider responses, context/compaction management, session persistence, tool execution. The TS prime-agent remains the parity ground truth; codex is a design reference. Cache-prefix stability is first-class: never adopt a pattern without checking its effect on the cacheable prefix.

lanes.types: Port the shared contract crate `pa-types` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/types (branch lane/contract-types). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/ai/src/types.ts (read in full) and the session JSONL format used by ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/core (messages.ts, agent-traces.ts, session-manager.ts). Also port daemon wire protocol message shapes from ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/daemon. Deliverable: serde Rust types + (de)serialization for AI messages, content blocks, tool calls/outputs, usage, stream events, session JSONL entries, daemon protocol messages. Verifier: capture real session JSONL from ~/.prime/agent (sessions live there) and write round-trip tests deserializing real captured lines losslessly. cargo test must pass on real captured data.
lanes.ai: Port the provider crate `pa-ai` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/ai (branch lane/ai-providers). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/ai/src — types.ts, providers/*.ts (anthropic, openai-completions, openai-responses*, google*, amazon-bedrock, mistral, faux, azure, register-builtins), utils/, env-api-keys.ts. pa-types on main may be incomplete; define needed message types locally in pa-ai with a note for later unification. Deliverable: provider trait + registry, streaming clients matching TS semantics (usage accounting, stream failure/retry, overflow, json-parse tolerance), faux provider. Verifier: faux-provider unit tests mirroring TS test semantics + a live differential test against the prime-inference endpoint (model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash; credentials already configured on this box) comparing assistant text and usage accounting with the TS product.
lanes.agent: Port the agent loop crate `pa-agent` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/agent (branch lane/agent-loop). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts, agent.ts, types.ts, proxy.ts (read all in full). Preserve exact semantics: max-turn behavior, tool-call dispatch/sequencing, partial stream handling, error propagation, abort/interrupt. Define a minimal local `ModelStream` trait + faux scripted provider for tests (documented for later unification with pa-ai). Verifier: tests replaying scripted tool-call conversations through the loop: normal turn, parallel tool calls, tool error, provider stream failure mid-turn with retry, user abort mid-stream, max iterations.
lanes.tui: Port the TUI crate `pa-tui` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/tui (branch lane/tui) using ratatui + crossterm. Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/tui/src (editor.ts, tui.ts, keys.ts, utils.ts, markdown.ts, autocomplete.ts, components/*, keybindings.ts, stdin-buffer.ts) and ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive. The interactive agent view is the most important surface; match layout, themes, configurable keybindings with TS DEFAULT_* defaults, editor behavior (history, kill ring, paste, undo, word ops), markdown rendering, autocomplete, loading/status, fullscreen/scrollback. Drive against a headless session-message stream trait you define so the same UI renders history JSONL and live events. Verifier: tmux tests — 80x24 tmux session renders a captured session from ~/.prime/agent in your TUI; capture pane; compare structure with the TS product rendering the same session. Include the tmux test script under tests/. Type text, backspace, arrows, ctrl+o, escape must behave like TS.
lanes.core-tools: Port tool implementations into `pa-core` (tool modules) in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/core-tools (branch lane/core-tools). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/ — bash.ts, edit.ts, edit-diff.ts, ipython.ts (tool side), code-preview.ts, file-mutation-queue.ts, path-utils.ts, render-utils.ts, truncate.ts, output-accumulator.ts, tool-definition-wrapper.ts, index.ts (read in full). Deliverable: tool definitions with exact model-facing names/JSON schemas (bash, edit, ipython; internal rename/stdout), file mutation queue, truncation rules, result rendering rules. Verifier: golden/differential tests vs the TS product for a corpus of >=20 real cases (fuzzy edits, file-not-found, bash timeouts, ipython outputs), asserting identical tool result text, truncation boundaries, and diff rendering.
lanes.core-kernel: Port the RLM kernel layer into `pa-core` (kernel module) in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/core-kernel (branch lane/core-kernel). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/core/kernel/ (repl-manager.ts, bootstrap.ts, shared.ts) and core/rlm-runtime.ts; plus installed skill contracts at ~/.local/share/prime-agent/releases/*/skills/*/SKILL.md. Deliverable: persistent IPython kernel lifecycle (spawn jupyter kernel over zeromq, execute cells, capture rich outputs, state across turns), the RLM surface injected into the kernel (rlm.*, agent_message, agent_observe, harness), persistence/revival semantics on kernel crash. Verifier: integration tests spawning a real `python -m ipykernel`: define variables across separate turns, kill -9 the kernel, verify restart-and-revive matches TS behavior (unserializable objects dropped and reported), cell outputs match the TS product for same code.
lanes.daemon: Redesign and port the daemon into `pa-daemon` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/daemon (branch lane/daemon). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/daemon* and modes/session-worker, plus core/session-manager.ts and core/session-lease.ts (read in full). Deliverable per ARCHITECTURE.md: supervisor process spawning one worker per active session, restart+backoff supervision, append-only session store on disk (same session store layout as the TS product), client attach/detach (sessions survive TUI exit), wire protocol with version/capability negotiation from the TS daemon protocol. Verifier: integration test script: start supervisor headlessly, create session worker running a scripted faux session, send messages, verify persistence; kill -9 supervisor, restart, reattach, verify history and queue state intact. Run under tmux; capture panes as PR evidence.
lanes.cli: Port the CLI crate `pa-cli` in worktree ~/lane-worktrees/cli (branch lane/cli). Source: ~/prime-agent/packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts and src/cli/*.ts (daemon-command.ts and siblings — read ALL in full, including every flag, interdependency, env var, and mode selection: interactive default, --print/-p headless, --json, --mode, --export, autonomous flags, --continue/--resume, session naming/fork, provider/model selection, skills/extensions flags). Deliverable: a clap-based `prime-agent` binary whose arg surface matches the TS product exactly (same flags, same shorthands, same semantics, same error messages where user-visible). Runtime behavior that depends on other crates (pa-core/pa-daemon/pa-ai) that are not merged yet: implement what you can standalone now (version, flag validation, config/env handling, help text) and define a clean internal API boundary (e.g. a `run(mode: Mode, opts)` entrypoint) with real typed options so crates plug in at merge time. Do NOT fake behavior with stub output; where a subsystem is missing, produce a clear typed error and a TODO-free integration plan in the PR description. Verifier: differential CLI tests vs the TS binary — a test script (committed under crates/pa-cli/tests/) that runs a corpus of CLI invocations (help, --version, invalid flags, flag validation errors, daemon subcommand usage, --print with missing model errors, etc.) against BOTH `prime-agent` (TS) and your Rust binary in a sandbox dir, and asserts matching exit codes / usage text / error text (normalize version numbers and binary name). All assertions must pass before you open the PR.
